subject: Residual covariances in moderated mediation with latent variables (indProd)

messages.author: f2b4ea1ef2b51d80
messages.subject: Residual covariances in moderated mediation with latent variables (indProd)
parts:
Hi everyone,

I am trying to run a moderated mediation with a latent interaction defined by (A) a five-item scale and (B) a 3-item scale. I have used indProd with match = FALSE and double-mean centering.
I am struggling understanding how residual covariances should be specified in the model, I would appreciate much anyone's help.

In particular, I have found other posts indicating that the latent interaction should covary with all the possible products created by indProd, is that correct?

latent_interaction ~~ item_A1.itemB1 + item_A1.itemB2 + item_A1.itemB3 + item_A1.itemB4 + item_A1.itemB5 + item_A2.itemB1 ... etc

Or, do the products need to covary among them all, for the same item, for example:

item_A1.itemB1 ~~ item_A1.itemB2 + item_A1.itemB3 + item_A1.itemB4 + item_A1.itemB5
item_A1.itemB2 ~~ item_A1.itemB3 + item_A1.itemB4 + item_A1.itemB5
item_A1.itemB3 ~~ item_A1.itemB4 + item_A1.itemB5
item_A1.itemB4 ~~ item_A1.itemB5
item_A2.itemB1 ~~ item_A2.itemB2 ... etc ?

Thank you in advance for anyone's attention and help.
Emanuele

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: Residual covariances in moderated mediation with latent variables (indProd)
parts:
The product terms become the indicators of the interaction factor, so change the ~~ to =~ in your first line:

latent_interaction =~ item_A1.itemB1 + item_A1.itemB2 + item_A1.itemB3 + item_A1.itemB4 + item_A1.itemB5 + item_A2.itemB1 ... etc

(You said that A had 5 items and B had 3 items, but this line of syntax suggests the other way around.)
Then the rule for residual covariances, in the absence of matching, is to allow a residual covariance for every pair of product indicators that share a term. So, for example, your next line of code:
item_A1.itemB1 ~~ item_A1.itemB2 + item_A1.itemB3 + item_A1.itemB4 + item_A1.itemB5

does the job for product terms containing item_A1.
If A has 3 items, then you will need 2 more lines like this, one for A2 and one for A3.

That should specify the 15 residual covariances (3 x 5) that the no-matching strategy entails.

--Ed Rigdon

messages.author: 5d4f9e7f97c21008
messages.subject: Re: Residual covariances in moderated mediation with latent variables (indProd)
parts:
Yes, that's the correct set of covariances for the A items, you also need to include residual covariances for the B items (e.g. all items with B1 covary). This can result in a LOT of parameters in the model, for this reason I'd recommend constraining covariances related to the same item to equality (e.g. all the covariances for the A1 items are constrained to equality). There's a discussion of that in this paper: https://doi.org/10.3390/
psych3030024 

Alex
